selectionSummary: Selected developments are South Korea's parliamentary budget pitch, a warning about northern Ethiopia's health system, and the closing US midterm campaign. Selection is editorial judgment, not an objective ranking.

snapshot.summary: Governments and voters confronted the gap between headline growth and everyday security: Korea debated how to invest a chip windfall, Ethiopia faced threats to basic care, and US candidates competed over affordability.
connections: Public spending choices influence who benefits from economic growth and who receives essential services.
Campaign promises, budget proposals and humanitarian warnings are different kinds of evidence; none is a completed outcome.
uncertainties: The Korean budget still required parliamentary approval.
US reports updated after the cutoff are used only for bounded, corroborated campaign developments; later broadcasts and election outcomes are excluded.

stories.title: Lee seeks approval for South Korea's record budget and AI investment
stories.summary: President Lee urged parliament to approve an 820.9 trillion won budget for 2027, including 21.3 trillion won for AI-related investment. The proposal raised questions about regional distribution, defence priorities and debt.
stories.whyItMatters: A major chip producer's spending choices affect technology capacity, economic resilience and the distribution of growth.
stories.selectionRationale: A major fiscal proposal brought before parliament with implications beyond the technology sector.
stories.evidenceNote: Three separately authored reports corroborate the proposed figures. Spending remains proposed; dollar conversions and forecast export milestones are omitted.

stories.title: WHO warns that violence is pushing northern Ethiopia's health system toward collapse
stories.summary: Tedros warned that fighting and attacks on civilians were worsening shortages and obstructing medical deliveries. Local reporting supplied witness accounts, while responsibility and casualty totals remained incompletely verified.
stories.whyItMatters: Loss of access to emergency, maternal and routine care can multiply the human cost of conflict.
stories.selectionRationale: A serious warning about essential services in a conflict with growing civilian consequences.
stories.evidenceNote: The reports share Tedros's statement, so repetition is not independent verification of his assessment. Addis Standard adds its own witness reporting; casualty estimates and perpetrator claims remain attributed.

commonFacts.text: Tedros warned that violence was worsening an already fragile health system in northern Ethiopia.

stories.title: US midterm campaigns close with affordability and congressional power at stake
stories.summary: Candidates made their final pitches before the November 3 vote. Economic grievances competed with partisan attacks, while analysts questioned how quickly proposed policies could lower household costs.
stories.whyItMatters: Control of Congress would shape the remaining two years of Trump's presidency and the government's policy choices.
stories.selectionRationale: The final campaign day in an election with substantial domestic and international consequences.
stories.evidenceNote: The selected wire pages later incorporated material beyond the Paris cutoff. This edition uses only the election schedule, policy stakes and corroborated daytime campaign themes; late Fox appearances, subsequent strikes and results are excluded.
